actual_scope: Classify full-rank integer lattices invariant at each stage of two opposite rational half-up rounded shears; prove the exact integer-product existence criterion for nonintegral slopes.
scope_change_reason: The source PR1848 explicitly leaves closure under intervening updates open. This is a new written precision-interface theorem with bounded exact corroboration, rather than a proof-assistant formalization or an audit of its cancellation theorem.
bottleneck_link: A correlated source lattice can justify a precision policy only if the actual rounded updates preserve it. The criterion rules out one fixed proper lattice for generic nonintegral shear pairs; physical caller binding and the five selected assumptions remain open.
stop_rule: Stop at the first proved closure criterion and its finite corroboration; package it without extending to affine, changing-stage or nonlinear domains.
evidence: PROOF.md supplies the all-rational proof. verify.py compares the criterion with complete finite-period literal executions for 75 Hermite lattices and 39 slopes, then checks nonintegral slope pairs and semantic/invalid-input controls.
